description: Metadata in the App Router allows you to define head configuration elements (e.g. title, description, open graph tags) using static metadata objects or dynamic generateMetadata functions. It is designed to be fully static-analysis friendly, and can only be exported from Server Component layouts or pages.

constraints.title: Do Not Export Metadata from Client Components
constraints.problem: Exporting export const metadata or generateMetadata() from a Client Component causes compilation errors or is ignored by Next.js at build time.
constraints.whyItMatters: Next.js parses metadata at build-time and server-side render time to stream search-engine readable tags inside the HTML header before hydration. Because Client Components run primarily on the client, they cannot participate in this initial server-side head composition process.
forbiddenPatterns: export const metadata = { ... } in a file containing 'use client'
export async function generateMetadata() { ... } in a file containing 'use client'
allowedPatterns: Exporting metadata strictly from layout.tsx or page.tsx Server Components
Updating client metadata dynamically using browser APIs inside useEffect or third-party libraries (e.g. react-helmet-async) if server meta is not required
productionRisks: Omitted metadata on critical paths, degrading SEO ranking and Open Graph social sharing
Corrupted page headers due to ignored dynamic configurations
architectureImplications: Separates content headers (meta) from component layout state
optimizationGuidance: Deduplicate dynamic data fetches inside generateMetadata() as Next.js automatically dedupes overlapping fetch calls
quickFixes: Remove the metadata export from the Client Component, or shift the metadata declaration to the parent server-side layout.tsx/page.tsx
architectureSuggestions: Keep layout metadata highly generic, override detailed tags dynamically using generateMetadata() inside individual leaf page.tsx components

invalid: 'use client'; export const metadata = { title: 'Dashboard' }; export default function Dashboard() { return <main>Content</main>; }
valid: // in page.tsx: export const metadata = { title: 'Dashboard' }; export default function Page() { return <DashboardClientComponent />; }

constraints.title: Avoid Fetch Duplication Inside Dynamic generateMetadata and Pages
constraints.problem: Fetching the same dataset twice (once in generateMetadata and once in page.tsx) using uncached non-fetch drivers (like standard ORM queries) causes database request waterfalls.
constraints.whyItMatters: Next.js automatically deduplicates fetch() requests with the same signature. However, if you are querying databases directly (e.g. using Prisma, Mongoose, or raw pg sockets) inside generateMetadata() and again inside page.tsx, these queries are not cached by default. This causes twice the database load per page view.
forbiddenPatterns: Executing direct un-memoized db.select() queries inside generateMetadata() and page.tsx for the exact same database records
allowedPatterns: Wrapping raw database query functions in React.cache() to deduplicate data fetching during request lifecycle
Using Next.js fetch() with standard caching configuration for data API endpoints
productionRisks: Increased page render latency (TTFB) due to duplicate sequential SQL calls
Higher cost on serverless databases (e.g. Neon, Supabase) due to redundant query counts
architectureImplications: Necessitates implementing a cached data access layer (DAL) using React's cache()
Enforces clean caching boundaries around custom ORM database fetches
optimizationGuidance: Always wrap non-fetch database query adapters in React.cache() to ensure they resolve exactly once per user request
quickFixes: Wrap the database query function with React.cache: const getCachedItem = cache(async (id) => { return db.getItem(id); })
architectureSuggestions: Establish a solid Data Access Layer (DAL) separating database calls into dedicated cached services consumed transparently by both metadata resolvers and render pages

{item.name}

import { cache } from 'react'; const getItem = cache(async (id) => db.getItem(id)); export async function generateMetadata({ params }) { const item = await getItem(params.id); return { title: item.title }; } export default async function Page({ params }) { const item = await getItem(params.id); return
{item.name}
; }
